subject.title: feat(channels/acp): support ACP bindings for direct-message peers

question: Should this PR publish openclaw/plugin-sdk/direct-peer-binding as a supported public SDK subpath, or should the helper stay private/Telegram-local until a broader channel API need is approved?
rationale: A plugin SDK subpath is a compatibility contract and this branch has only one immediate consumer, while the runtime behavior also changes routing for already-accepted Telegram direct/dm ACP configs.

options.title: Keep Helper Private For Now
options.body: Localize the helper to Telegram or an internal channel file, fix the docs snippet, and revisit a public SDK subpath when another channel needs the same contract.

options.title: Approve The SDK Subpath
options.body: Accept direct-peer binding as a supported plugin SDK API, keep the export, and make the PR carry the corresponding public-contract expectations.

options.title: Pause Or Replace The Branch
options.body: Close or pause this branch if maintainers want the direct-DM fix but not the broader SDK/API shape in this contribution.

recommendation.title: Keep Helper Private For Now
recommendation.body: Localize the helper to Telegram or an internal channel file, fix the docs snippet, and revisit a public SDK subpath when another channel needs the same contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent plugin SDK public-contract and Telegram channel history makes this the strongest routing candidate for the API/product decision.
